newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end up on EMU hopes,Fiat group firm.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end up on EMU hopes,Fiat group firm.

text.p: Italian shares closed higher on Wednesday, boosted by firmer Fiat group stocks and on comments by Treasury Minister Ciampi that European Union forecasts on the Italian economy confirmed Italy would be in shape to join a single currency from the start, traders said.

Industrial giant Fiat SpA closed 5.08 percent up at 4,406 lire in strong volume of nearly 20 million shares. Energy group ENI was the most traded stock, ending 1.22 percent up at 7,480 lire with over 28 million shares changing hands.

The all-share Mibtel index ended 1.40 percent higher at 10,035 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 1.44 percent up at 15,111. Total traded volume was estimated at some 900 billion lire against Tuesday's 700 billion lire.

Other stocks in the Fiat empire also performed well. Agnelli family holding companies IFI and IFIL registered strong advances, with IFI preferential shares up over 9.0 percent at 14,298 and IFIL up over 4.0 percent at 4,218.
Fiat units Snia Bpd amd Sorin Biomedica were again the subjects of interest. Sorin heads up the bio-engineering activities of chemical holding Snia Bpd.
Snia Bpd closed 2.81 percent up at 1,356 lire and Sorin closed 3.04 percent higher at 5,395.
Fiat's auto components unit Magneti Marelli also put on over six percent to 1,670.
Healthy buying interest was also seen in the telecoms sector where Telecom Italia gained 3.43 percent to 3,647 lire and mobile phone operator TIM rose 0.58 percent to 3,295, both in strong volume.
Olivetti put on a modest 0.14 percent to 442.1 lire but Carlo De Benedetti's Cir industrial holding group rose 1.73 percent to 754.8.
Agro-industrial group Montedison, seeing better margins in the second half, gained 1.25 percent to 1,053 lire.
